Given the sets $Y={△,◻,♣,♡}$ and  $Z={△,◻,♡,♢,♠}$ shown above, find $Z∖Y.$
questions.worked_solution:
The difference $Z∖Y$ consists of all the elements that are in $Z$ but not $Y.$ To represent $Z∖Y,$ we will shade in all the area that is contained in $Z$ but not $Y.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071857/assets/45a15beb8833e2974706a04b0cdfd81dcdda4b92323f0c092683b9882e53b0ea.png)

The elements $♠$ and $♢$ are in $Z$  but not $Y.$

Therefore, the difference is

$$
Z∖Y={♠,♢}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Differences of Sets Given Verbally
questions.problem: Let $S$  be the set of all multiples of $2$ greater than $0$ and let $T$  be the set of all multiples of $4$ greater than $0.$ What is $T∖S?$
questions.worked_solution:
The multiples of $2$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
S={2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16,…}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $4$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
T={4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32,36,…}.
$$

Now, $T∖S$ is the *difference* of $T$ and $S,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $T$ but *not* in $S.$

The elements of $T$ that are also in $S$ are $4,8,12,16,$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $4$). So, we must remove these elements from $T.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T∖S & ={4,8,12,16,…}-{2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16,…} \\  & =∅.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $A$  be the set of all multiples of $3$ greater than $0$ and let $B$  be the set of all multiples of $4$ greater than $0.$ What is $B-A?$
questions.worked_solution:
The multiples of $3$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
A=\{3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24,…\}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $4$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
B=\{4,8,12,16,20,24,…\}.
$$

Now, $B-A$ is the *difference* of $B$ and $A,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $B$ but *not* in $A.$

The elements of $B$ that are also in $A$ are $12,24,$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $12$). So, we must remove these elements from $B.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B-A & =\{4,8,12,16,20,24,…\}-\{3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24,…\} \\  & =\{4,8,16,20,…\}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $E$  be the set of all non-negative integer powers of $2$ and let $F$  be  the set of all non-negative integer powers of $4.$  What is $F-E?$
questions.worked_solution:
The powers of $2$ that are greater or equal to $1$ are

$$
E={1,2,4,8,16,32,64,…}.
$$

Likewise, the powers of $4$ that are greater or equal to $1$ are

$$
F={1,4,16,64,256,…}.
$$

Now, $F-E$ is the *difference* of $F$ and $E,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $F$ but *not* in $E.$

All elements of $F$ are also in $E.$  So, we must remove these elements from $F.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F-E & ={1,4,16,64,256,…}-{1,2,4,8,16,32,64,…} \\  & =∅.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $C$  be the set of all multiples of $10$ greater than $0$ and let $D$  be the the set of all multiples of $5$ greater than $0.$ What is $C∖D?$
questions.worked_solution:
The multiples of $10$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
C=\{10,20,30,40,50,60,70,…\}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $5$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
D=\{5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,70,75,…\}.
$$

Now, $C∖D$ is the *difference* of $C$ and $D,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $C$ but *not* in $D.$

The elements of $C$ that are also in $D$ are $10,20,30,40,$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $10$). So, we must remove these elements from $C.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}C∖D & =C-D \\  & =\{10,20,30,40,50,60,70,…\}-\{5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,50,55,60,65,70,75,…\} \\  & =∅.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Difference of Sets Without a Venn Diagram
canonical_examples.problem: Given the sets $X = \{ 2, 5, 7, 8 \},$ $Y = \{ 1, 3, 5 \},$ and $Z = \{ 2, 4, 6, 8 \},$ find $X \setminus Y,$ $Y \setminus Z,$ and $Z \setminus X.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The set $X \setminus Y$ is the set of all elements belonging to $X$ but *not* $Y.$ Note that the element $5 \in Y$ is also in $X,$ so we must remove it. Hence, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}X∖Y & =X-Y \\  & ={2,5,7,8}-{1,3,5} \\  & ={2,7,8}.\end{aligned}
$$

The set $Y \setminus Z$ is the set of all elements belonging to $Y$ but *not* $Z.$ Note that none of the elements of $Y$ are in $Z.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Y∖Z & =Y-Z \\  & ={1,3,5}-{2,4,6,8} \\  & ={1,3,5}.\end{aligned}
$$

The set $Z \setminus X$ is the set of all elements belonging to $Z$ but *not* $X.$ Note that the elements $2,8 \in Z$ are also in $X,$ so we must remove them. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Z∖X & =Z-X \\  & ={2,4,6,8}-{2,5,7,8} \\  & ={4,6}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding Differences of Sets Given Verbally
canonical_examples.problem: Let $A$ be the set of all multiples of $4$ that are greater than $0$ and let $B$ be the set of all multiples of $6$ that are greater than $0.$ What is $A \setminus B?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The multiples of $4$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
A = \{ 4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32, 36 \ldots \}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $6$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
B = \{ 6,12,18,24,30,36,\ldots \}.
$$

Now, $A \setminus B$ is the *difference* of $A$ and $B,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $A$ but *not* in $B.$

The elements of $A$ that are also in $B$ are $12, 24, 36$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $12$). So, we must remove these elements from $A.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A∖B & =A-B \\  & ={4,8,12,16,20,24,28,32,36,…}-{6,12,18,24,30,36,…} \\  & ={4,8,16,20,28,32,…}.\end{aligned}
$$
